subject: Computer Networking
title: Wi-Fi Changes Everything
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wi-Fi Changes Everything.

hook.text: In 1999, Apple put a wireless card in the iBook. Steve Jobs browsed the web while walking across a stage.

buildup.text: Wi-Fi used the 802.11 standard to send data over radio waves. No cables, no drilling, instant connectivity.

discovery.text: Coffee shops, airports, and homes all added Wi-Fi. By 2005, wireless internet was expected everywhere.

twist.text: Early Wi-Fi was slow and insecure. WEP encryption was cracked within years of its release.

climax.text: Wi-Fi 6 now delivers gigabit speeds wirelessly. The standard keeps evolving to handle more devices and more data.

punchline.text: Wi-Fi untethered the internet. The wire became optional.

details.summary: Wi-Fi, standardized as IEEE 802.11 in 1997, freed computers from physical network cables. It evolved from 2 Mbps to multi-gigabit speeds and became ubiquitous in homes, offices, airports, and cafes. Wi-Fi transformed where and how people use the internet more than any other access technology.
details.whyItMatters: Wi-Fi untethered computing from cables and made internet access pervasive. It transformed workplaces, created the mobile workforce, and made connectivity an expected utility everywhere.
takeaways: Wi-Fi was standardized as IEEE 802.11 in 1997
Speeds evolved from 2 Mbps to multi-gigabit
Wi-Fi made internet access ubiquitous in daily life

faq.question: How has Wi-Fi evolved through its generations?
faq.answer: From 802.11b at 11 Mbps through 802.11g, n, ac, and ax, each generation increased speed, range, and capacity. Wi-Fi 6 added efficiency for dense environments. Wi-Fi 7 pushes toward 40 Gbps. Each generation addressed the growing demand for wireless bandwidth.

faq.question: Why is Wi-Fi more popular than wired connections for end users?
faq.answer: Convenience. No cables means any device can connect anywhere in range. Laptops, phones, tablets, and IoT devices are all wireless-first. While wired connections offer better performance, the mobility and simplicity of Wi-Fi make it the preferred choice for most users.
